create.name: East Bay Meditation Center
create.bio:
East Bay Meditation Center is a Buddhist practice community in downtown Oakland, California, set up in 2007 to give a spiritual home to people of colour, LGBTQI practitioners and people with disabilities, groups that had often felt on the margins of American meditation halls. Its teaching draws mainly on Buddhist insight practice in the spirit of socially engaged Buddhism, alongside other contemplative traditions, and today everyone is welcome. It began in a small storefront, moved to a larger hall in 2012 and has since been looking for a permanent building of its own.

Most of the centre's life happens in weekly practice groups, several of them for particular communities: a BIPOC Sangha that has met on Thursdays since late 2006, an Alphabet Sangha led by LGBTQIA+ teachers, a peer-led midday sitting group and others, meeting in person on 17th Street, on Zoom or both. It also runs daylongs and multi-week classes, a year-long practice programme and a two-year training for people who lead Dharma groups. Everything is offered on a dana basis, so no one is turned away for lack of money, and the hall is wheelchair accessible and fragrance free.

courses.title: Finding Liberation in Relationship
courses.description: A four-week online evening class with Dawn Haney and René Rivera that brings Buddhist meditation and body awareness to friendships, partnerships and community life. Offered by donation, with suggested tiers.

courses.title: Spiritual Teacher and Leadership Training
courses.description: A two-year training for committed practitioners who lead or coordinate Dharma groups, with monthly meetings, two week-long residential retreats and shorter retreats. Guiding teachers give the core curriculum.

free_resources.title: BIPOC Sangha
free_resources.description: A weekly Thursday meditation and Dharma group for Black, Indigenous and People of Color, meeting in person and online, open to beginners and long-time meditators. Offered on a dana basis.

free_resources.title: Alphabet Sangha
free_resources.description: A weekly practice group with guided meditation and Dharma talks from LGBTQIA+ teachers, for queer, trans and same-gender-loving practitioners. Some meetings are hybrid.

free_resources.title: Midday Sangha
free_resources.description: A peer-led Wednesday lunchtime group for silent sitting and Dharma discussion, mostly on Zoom with an in-person meeting once a month. Drop in for as long as suits you.

sprint.held: Dropped by the owner (10 Nov 2026): leave out. Previous hold: Owner decision needed: the centre frames its dharma practice strongly around social justice (a published 'stance on Gaza' post, a white-identity group, a Practice in Transformative Action programme for organisers). It is a meditation centre first, but the owner should decide whether this counts as political-centred.
